reasons: Rule applies: Section 1.4 is the operative grant of access/use rights to us (the customer) over HDI's system and administration tools, and it names only "the Company" — no affiliates, no contractors, and no written-notice mechanic to add them.

Classification is correct: the clause fails the fallback on a material term (affiliate coverage on written notice is absent), so "deviation" rather than "compliant" is right; Section 10.3's successors-and-assigns language only partially supports the transferability element and does not cure the affiliate/contractor gap.

Redline is actionable and directionally correct for us: it appends affiliate/contractor/successor coverage to the Section 1.4 grant and carves those parties out of the "no other person" limitation, expanding our rights without adding obligations on us or new obligations on HDI beyond who may exercise existing rights.

Deterministic changed-character ratios (0.705 / 0.681) are explained by appending a single coverage sentence to short paragraphs and by an in-line carve-out; the underlying edits are insertions that preserve the original wording, so the advisory minimality flags are not disqualifying.

Comment is accurate, concise, cites the playbook position, and offers the affiliates-on-written-notice fallback with the required [Playbook] prefix; the rationale's characterisation of Section 10.3 as an affirmative exclusion (rather than a standard no-third-party-beneficiary clause) is somewhat strong and its "walk-away" framing overstates the position, but this does not change the deviation outcome or the validity of the edit.
